issues.body:
The new block is placed after the `binary GOO` / `worst-case-optimal (LFTJ)` label is chosen and gates only on `patterns.len() >= 3 && crate::dp::active().is_some()` — not on `bgp_uses_binary(&patterns)`.

DPccp is only reachable on the binary path: `eval_flat_conjunctive` (exec.rs:4858) dispatches `bgp_uses_binary(patterns)` -> `eval_bgp_binary`, and the `#[cfg(feature = "dp-planner")] if let Some(cfg) = crate::dp::active()` / `eval_bgp_dp` block lives inside `eval_bgp_binary` (exec.rs:6953). A cyclic BGP takes the `else` arm (`eval_bgp` -> LFTJ) and never touches `dp::plan`.

So for a cyclic 3+-pattern BGP the explain-json operator label and the ANALYZE trace label read `BGP [worst-case-optimal (LFTJ)] (3 patterns, 0 filters) [DPccp may execute; displayed tree is a greedy replay, not an execution record]` — where DPccp definitively cannot execute, and the displayed order is an LFTJ global variable order, not a greedy replay at all. Both halves of the sentence are wrong on that shape.

explain.rs gets this right by construction: the LFTJ branch returns early at explain.rs:289-313, so the note is only written in the binary branch. exec.rs::trace_label lacks the equivalent guard.

This errs toward over-warning rather than hiding a divergence, which is why it is minor rather than major — but the whole point of the change is honest disclosure, so an inaccurate disclosure undercuts it.
issues.title: trace_label appends the DPccp note to cyclic (LFTJ) BGPs where DPccp cannot run, and calls the LFTJ tree a "greedy replay"

issues.body:
Both new tests only assert the note is PRESENT on a DP-eligible BGP. `accept_header_requests_explain` asserts the greedy label for the 2-pattern JOIN_QUERY with `contains`, which passes whether or not the note is also emitted.

As a result the condition guarding the note (`patterns.len() >= 3`, and the missing `bgp_uses_binary` check above) has no test that goes red when the note is emitted too widely — which is exactly the failure mode present in exec.rs today.
issues.fix_hint: Add one assertion that the note is absent where DPccp cannot apply: `assert!(!body.contains("DPccp may execute"))` for the 2-pattern JOIN_QUERY, and ideally for a 3-pattern CYCLIC (triangle) BGP once the exec.rs guard is fixed. Both are cheap additions to the existing spawned-server tests.
issues.title: No negative test pins the ABSENCE of the DPccp note, so over-disclosure regressions are unguarded

issues.body: `dp-planner` gets crates/sparq-server/tests/dp_planner_default.rs and `algebra-rewrite` gets crates/sparq-server/tests/algebra_rewrite_default.rs, both of which fail to compile if the forwarding edge to sparq-engine is broken. `antijoin-static-decline`, added to the default set in the same commit, has no equivalent witness, so silently dropping `antijoin-static-decline = ["sparq-engine/antijoin-static-decline"]` (or the default-set entry) would not be caught by any server-side test — while the README and SKILL would keep claiming CLI parity.
issues.fix_hint: Either add a matching one-test tripwire (same shape as dp_planner_default.rs, gated `#![cfg(feature = "antijoin-static-decline")]`, referencing whatever engine symbol the feature exposes), or note explicitly in the feature comment that this edge is covered only by the engine's `sparq-engine (antijoin-static-decline)` feature-matrix leg.
issues.title: Newly-defaulted antijoin-static-decline has no forwarding tripwire, unlike its two siblings

issues.body: Line 5 reads "This file is gated on the server feature so deliberate lean builds remain valid", while the actual attribute is `#![cfg(feature = "dp-planner")]`. "the server feature" reads as the `server` feature, which is a different (and also real) feature of this crate. The very next sentence gets it right ("Removing `dp-planner` from `default` therefore silently skips it"), so this is only wording.
issues.fix_hint: Say "gated on the server's `dp-planner` forwarding feature" to match the sibling algebra_rewrite_default.rs phrasing.
issues.title: Module doc says the file is "gated on the server feature" but the gate is dp-planner

issues.body: The SKILL blockquote defers the actual fix ("Until DP-aware explain rendering lands, EXPLAIN labels a DP-eligible BGP as a greedy replay") without a tracking id, and neither the README bullet nor the Cargo.toml comment references one. AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md hygiene puts future work in a bead, and every other deferral in these files carries an `sq-*` / `#NNNN` reference. verdict.summary:
Both round-1 majors are resolved and locally verified.

(1) EXPLAIN/plan divergence: the PR takes option (b) from the prior fix_hint — disclosure rather than DP-aware rendering. explain.rs:324 writes a NOTE scoped to the binary-BGP branch, and exec.rs trace_label appends "[DPccp may execute; displayed tree is a greedy replay, not an execution record]", which reaches both the ANALYZE text trace (exec.rs:4605) and the explain-json operator labels (explain_json.rs:257/:265 via trace_label_pub). Two new server tests pin this under the DEFAULT feature set with a 3-pattern DP-eligible BGP, closing the round-1 CI blind spot (JOIN_QUERY was 2 patterns, below dp::plan's >=3 gate). Verified: `cargo test -p sparq-server --test explain_metrics` 11/11 pass; the assertions target the exact new strings, so they go red if the note is dropped — not vacuous.

(2) Parity overclaim: `antijoin-static-decline` joins the server default set, making the plan-affecting set exactly {dp-planner, algebra-rewrite, antijoin-static-decline} — identical to sparq-cli/Cargo.toml:146. The CLI's default set (mmap, mimalloc, dict-spill, jsonld) and its other engine-forwarding features are not plan-affecting, so the claim now holds; the wording is also tightened from "same plans" to the checkable "join ordering and rewrite/anti-join evaluation ordering".

Minors 3/4 are fixed by rewording (the tripwire doc discloses that a default-set removal silently skips it and that only the forwarding edge is enforced; the test doc no longer claims DP acceptance). Minor 5 is documented in Cargo.toml/README/SKILL, noting accurately that DP enumeration does not poll QueryBudget: dp.rs has no deadline check and http.rs:6617's `timeout + TIMEOUT_GRACE` returns 503 without aborting the blocking task, so a bounded-CPU residual remains, now disclosed.

DPccp stays order-only on a commutative/associative natural join; both feature states compile warning-free; no existing label assertion breaks. Findings below are minor/nit.
